thought.text: I'm installing the Android SDK command-line tools and running `flutter pub get` in parallel since the app uses compileSdk 36, targetSdk 36, minSdk 24, and NDK 27.

reasoning_content:
The app is compiled with `compileSdk = flutter.compileSdkVersion` = 36, minSdk 24, targetSdk 36, ndkVersion 27.0.12077973.

So what's needed for the Android SDK is:
- platforms;android-36
- build-tools (for AGP 8.9.1: latest required is 35.0.0; AGP 8.9's default build tools is 35.0.0)
- platform-tools
- emulator
- NDK 27.0.12077973 (only if the build requires the NDK — objectbox's CMake/native? objectbox uses prebuilt libraries; flutter's build doesn't require the NDK unless there's native code. Actually `ndkVersion` is set, but NDK is only needed when native builds are performed. flutter_local_notifications uses prebuilt .so files, so no NDK needed. The Gradle build itself won't download the NDK unless it's used.)
- system-images for the emulator + AVD (a "ready-made virtual device").

Next, install Android SDK command-line tools. Download from dl.google.com/android/repository/commandlinetools-linux-11076708_latest.zip (or the latest version). Check the available versions — the "latest" link. Use the known stable URL: https://dl.google.com/android/repository/commandlinetools-linux-11076708_latest.zip (version 12). There might be newer ones (13114758 = v13?). As of 2025: commandlinetools-linux-13114758_latest.zip exists (v16?). Use the well-known 11076708 that reliably exists, or query the repository XML for the latest version. Let me query https://dl.google.com/android/repository/repository2-3.xml for the latest "commandlinetools-linux" entry. More simply: try a few known URLs.

sdkmanager license: yes | sdkmanager --licenses.

Next, create an AVD with avdmanager. System image: check what's available (android-34 or 35). `sdkmanager --list` is slow; use `--list` with a filter.

Download size: system image is around 1.5GB. RAM is 7.6GB — the emulator might just barely run; disk has 951G free.

Alright, let's proceed:
1. Download commandlinetools
2. Install SDK packages + licenses
3. flutter doctor
4. fvm flutter pub get
5. Build

While doing the SDK setup, in parallel start `fvm flutter pub get` (it doesn't depend on the Android SDK). Actually, does pub get also build the native objectbox part? No — objectbox_flutter_libs just downloads prebuilt .so files via pub; no native build at pub get time. pub get should be fine to run now.

action.command: cd /tmp && curl -sL --max-time 300 -o cmdtools.zip https://dl.google.com/android/repository/commandlinetools-linux-11076708_latest.zip && unzip -q cmdtools.zip && mkdir -p /opt/android-sdk/cmdline-tools && mv cmdline-tools /opt/android-sdk/cmdline-tools/latest && ls /opt/android-sdk/cmdline-tools/latest/bin | head
